proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a mode and condition on \((\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}independent\mbox{-}selection}\), the selected population blocks are fixed and the fitting errors retain their conditional laws.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}cells}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\mbox{-}inference\mbox{-}blocks}\), the primitive blocks used below are independent centered Gaussian blocks whenever independence is invoked.  Set
\[
 b_n=\log(nH_n),\qquad u_n=K\frac{\sqrt{b_n}}n,
\]
where constants depend only on the radii defining \(\mathcal C_n\).

We first construct one uniform event.  For every selected design \(X=\bar X+E\), a Gaussian net bound and balanced dimensions give \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K\sqrt n\) except on an event of conditional probability at most \(K(nH_n)^{-A}\), for any fixed \(A>0\).  A union bound is valid because the menus have bounded cardinality and there are only \(O(H_n)\) response vectors.  Weyl's inequality, the gap in \(\mathrm{ass{:}strong\mbox{-}spectrum}\), and the fixed-rank bound imply
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat X)\ge c_sn/2,\qquad
 \|\widehat X^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K/n,\qquad
 \|\widehat X^\dagger-\bar X^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Kn^{-3/2},
 \qquad \|\widehat P_X-P_X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Kn^{-1/2}.              \tag{1}
\]
Only the gap to zero is used, so repeated nonzero singular values are allowed.  The threshold in \(\mathrm{def{:}pcr\mbox{-}map}\) lies between the \(O(\sqrt n)\) noise singular values and the order-\(n\) signal singular values; thus (1) also proves rank recovery and excludes the fallback on this event.

For a generic selected PCR regression \(u=\bar X\gamma+e\), the exact identity
\[
 \widehat\gamma-\gamma
 =(\widehat P_{X,c}-P_{X,c})\gamma
 +\widehat X^\dagger e-\widehat X^\dagger E\gamma                 \tag{2}
\]
follows from \(\widehat X^\dagger X=\widehat P_{X,c}\).  Bounded means and (1) give \(\|\gamma\|_2\le K/\sqrt n\).  Conditional on \(X\), the response error is independent Gaussian and its retained projection has fixed rank; hence \(\|\widehat X^\dagger e\|_2\le K\sqrt{b_n}/n\).  The other terms in (2) are \(O(n^{-1})\).  Applying (2) to all regressions yields
\[
 \|\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n\|_2\le u_n,\quad
 \max_{\ell\le H_n}\|\widehat a_{n,\ell}-a_{n,\ell}\|_2\le u_n,\quad
 \|\widehat a_n-a_n\|_2\le u_n.                                     \tag{3}
\]

The same deterministic bounds give
\[
 \|\beta_n\|_2+\|a_n\|_2+\max_\ell\|a_{n,\ell}\|_2\le Kn^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\bar W_n^\top\beta_n\|_2\le K\sqrt n,                       \tag{4}
\]
\[
 \max_{m,\ell}\|p_{m,n,\ell}\|_2\le Kn^{-1/2},\quad
 \max_\ell\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2\le Kn^{-1/2},\quad
 \max_\ell\|q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2\le KH_nn^{-1/2}.              \tag{5}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 g_{n,\ell}=\{\Pi_n(a_n)^{\ell-1}\}^{\top}a_n
\]
for \(\ell\ge1\), so stable short recursion gives \(\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2\le K/\sqrt n\).  Product differentiation gives \(\|J_{n,\ell}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KH_n\).  Writing \(d_a=\widehat a_n-a_n\), telescoping powers and differentiating once more yield
\[
 \widehat g_{n,\ell}=g_{n,\ell}+J_{n,\ell}d_a+\rho_{n,\ell},\qquad
 \|\widehat g_{n,\ell}-g_{n,\ell}\|_2\le KH_nu_n,\qquad
 \|\rho_{n,\ell}\|_2\le KH_n^2u_n^2,                                 \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \|\widehat J_{n,\ell}-J_{n,\ell}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KH_n^2u_n.      \tag{7}
\]
The fitted powers remain bounded because their telescoping recursion is bounded by \(K\exp(KH_nu_n)=O(1)\) for \(H_n\le n^{1/8}\).

The centering is causal rather than definitional.  Direct transport gives
\[
 \theta_{n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n.
\]
The factor model, Hankel-rank condition, and recursive recovery transport the same conditional mean under the population recurrence and give
\[
 \theta_{n,\ell}=g_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n.            \tag{8}
\]
Unit recovery implies
\[
 \bar Y_n^{\top}p_{m,n,\ell}=\bar W_nh_{m,n,\ell},\qquad
 h_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell},\quad
 h_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=g_{n,\ell}.                                 \tag{9}
\]
Recursive recovery also gives
\[
 \bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\top}q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}
 =J_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n.                            \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, product differentiation writes the right side as
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
 (e_{L_n}^{\top}\Pi_n(a_n)^je_{L_n})
 \Pi_n(a_n)^{\ell-1-j}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n,
\]
and each summand is a recovered advanced terminal state.  The direct response-span condition supplies the analogous Riesz cancellation on the population coefficient subspace.

Write \(d_\beta=\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n\),
\[
 \delta_\beta=e_{y,n}-E_{Y,n}\beta_n,\qquad
 \delta_a=e_{\mathrm{rec},n}-E_{Z,\mathrm{rec},n}a_n,
\]
\[
 t_\ell=J_{n,\ell}d_a,\quad
 d_p=(\widehat P_Y-P_Y)p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell},\quad
 d_q=(\widehat P_Z-P_Z)q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}.
\]
Add the zero fitted-normal-equation corrections to the recursive PCR center, expand around (8), apply (9)--(10), and subtract the score in \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\).  The exact remainder is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 r_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}={}&
 t_\ell^\top\bar W_n^\top d_\beta+t_\ell^\top E_{W,n}^\top\beta_n
 +g_{n,\ell}^\top E_{W,n}^\top d_\beta+t_\ell^\top E_{W,n}^\top d_\beta\\
&+\rho_{n,\ell}^\top\bar W_n^\top\beta_n
 +\rho_{n,\ell}^\top\bar W_n^\top d_\beta
 +\rho_{n,\ell}^\top E_{W,n}^\top\beta_n
 +\rho_{n,\ell}^\top E_{W,n}^\top d_\beta\\
&-p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^\top E_{Y,n}d_\beta
 -q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^\top E_{Z,\mathrm{rec},n}d_a
 +d_p^\top\delta_\beta-d_p^\top\bar Y_nd_\beta-d_p^\top E_{Y,n}d_\beta\\
&+d_q^\top\delta_a-d_q^\top\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}d_a
 -d_q^\top E_{Z,\mathrm{rec},n}d_a .
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{11}
\]
From (1) and (5), \(\|d_p\|_2\le K/n\) and \(\|d_q\|_2\le KH_n/n\).  Conditional scalar Gaussian bounds, using the disjoint response cells, give
\[
 |d_p^\top\delta_\beta|\le K\sqrt{b_n}/n,\qquad
 |d_q^\top\delta_a|\le KH_n\sqrt{b_n}/n.                              \tag{12}
\]
Equations (3)--(7), the operator bounds, and (12), term by term in (11), imply
\[
 \max_{\ell\le H_n}|r_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}|
 \le K\left(\frac{H_nb_n}{n}+\frac{H_n^2b_n}{n^{3/2}}\right).         \tag{13}
\]
For example, the first and fifth terms are bounded by \((KH_nu_n)(Kn)u_n=KH_nb_n/n\) and \((KH_n^2u_n^2)(K\sqrt n)=KH_n^2b_n/n^{3/2}\); the two contractions in (12) prevent a spurious factor \(\sqrt n\).  Every other term is no larger.

In direct mode the same bilinear calculation has \(g=a_{n,\ell}\), derivative \(I\), and no \(\rho\) term.  It gives
\[
 \max_{\ell\le H_n}|r_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}|\le Kb_n/n.               \tag{14}
\]
Dividing (13)--(14) by the strictly positive floor \(s_{m,n,\ell}\ge c_vn^{-1/2}\) proves the stated rates.  After the Riesz cancellations, the remaining linear terms are exactly those in \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\).  They are a linear map of independent centered Gaussian cells, hence are exactly jointly Gaussian with covariance \(\Sigma_{m,n}\).  The event probability is uniform over the finite menus and class radii, and averaging over the selected layout preserves it.

Continue on the event established in \(\mathrm{thm{:}stacked\mbox{-}orthogonal\mbox{-}expansion}\), and put \(b_n=\log(nH_n)\) and \(w_n=\bar W_n^\top\beta_n\).  Independence and the score definition give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{\Sigma_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)}{\sigma_n^2}
={}&\|\beta_n\|_2^2a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}
 +(1+\|\beta_n\|_2^2)p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}p_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}\\
&+\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2^2
 \{\mathbf1\{\ell=k\}+a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}\},
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{15}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{\Sigma_{\mathrm{rec},n}(\ell,k)}{\sigma_n^2}
={}&\|\beta_n\|_2^2g_{n,\ell}^{\top}g_{n,k}
 +(1+\|\beta_n\|_2^2)p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}p_{\mathrm{rec},n,k}\\
&+(1+\|a_n\|_2^2)q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}q_{\mathrm{rec},n,k}.
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{16}
\]
The feasible construction replaces these coefficients by their fitted counterparts, uses observed \(W_n\), and equals
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_{m,n}
 =\widehat\sigma_n^2\widehat Q_{m,n}\widehat Q_{m,n}^{\top}\succeq0.
\]
Thus it is observable and positive semidefinite, including when singular.

The preceding PCR and companion bounds imply
\[
 \|W_n^\top\widehat\beta_n-w_n\|_2\le K\sqrt{b_n},
\]
\[
 \max_\ell\{\|\widehat p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}-p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2+
 \|\widehat q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}-q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2\}
 \le K\sqrt{b_n}/n,                                                    \tag{17}
\]
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widehat p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}-p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2
 \le KH_n\sqrt{b_n}/n.                                                 \tag{18}
\]
The actual recursive temporal representer has the exact three-piece perturbation
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}-q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}
={}&(\widehat Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\dagger\top}
       -\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\dagger\top})J_{n,\ell}^{\top}w_n\\
&+\widehat Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\dagger\top}J_{n,\ell}^{\top}
  (W_n^\top\widehat\beta_n-w_n)\\
&+\widehat Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\dagger\top}
  (\widehat J_{n,\ell}-J_{n,\ell})^{\top}W_n^\top\widehat\beta_n.
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{19}
\]
Its three terms are respectively
\[
 O(H_n/n),\qquad O(H_n\sqrt{b_n}/n),\qquad
 O(H_n^2\sqrt{b_n}/n^{3/2}),
\]
so their sum is \(O(H_n\sqrt{b_n}/n)\) when \(H_n\le n^{1/8}\).  Thus neither an oracle terminal block nor an oracle Jacobian has been substituted.

For any vectors \(x_\ell,x_k\) and perturbations \(d_\ell,d_k\),
\[
 |(x_\ell+d_\ell)^\top(x_k+d_k)-x_\ell^\top x_k|
 \le\|x_\ell\|_2\|d_k\|_2+\|x_k\|_2\|d_\ell\|_2+\|d_\ell\|_2\|d_k\|_2. \tag{20}
\]
Applying (20) to every Gram term in (15)--(16) gives, before variance estimation,
\[
 \max_{\ell,k}|\widehat K_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)-K_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)|
 \le K\sqrt{b_n}/n^{3/2},
\]
\[
 \max_{\ell,k}|\widehat K_{\mathrm{rec},n}(\ell,k)-K_{\mathrm{rec},n}(\ell,k)|
 \le KH_n^2\sqrt{b_n}/n^{3/2}.                                       \tag{21}
\]

For either pooled residual regression,
\[
 (I-\widehat P_X)u=v+(I-\widehat P_X)e,\qquad
 v=(I-\widehat P_X)\bar u,\qquad\|v\|_2\le K.
\]
Conditionally on the design, the squared Gaussian term divided by \(\sigma_n^2\) is chi-square with positive residual degrees of freedom of order \(n\); its cross term with \(v\) is Gaussian with bounded variance, and the leakage \(\|v\|_2^2\) divided by degrees of freedom is \(O(n^{-1})\).  Hence
\[
 \left|\widehat\sigma_n^2/\sigma_n^2-1\right|
 \le K\sqrt{b_n/n}.                                                    \tag{22}
\]
Combining (21)--(22), using \(|\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)|\le s_{m,n,\ell}s_{m,n,k}\), and dividing by \(s_{m,n,\ell}s_{m,n,k}\ge c_v^2/n\), proves
\[
 B_{\mathrm{dir},n}=O_{\Pr}(\sqrt{b_n/n}),\qquad
 B_{\mathrm{rec},n}=O_{\Pr}(H_n^2\sqrt{b_n/n}),                       \tag{23}
\]
where \(B_{m,n}\) denotes the maximum relative covariance error.

On \(B_{m,n}\le1/2\), write \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,\ell)=s_{m,n,\ell}^2(1+e_\ell)\).  Since \(|e_\ell|\le B_{m,n}\) and \(|\sqrt{1+x}-1|\le|x|\) for \(x\ge-1/2\),
\[
 t_{m,n}\le B_{m,n}.
\]
Adding and subtracting \(\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)/
(\widehat s_{m,n,\ell}\widehat s_{m,n,k})\), using the last inequality and the covariance Cauchy--Schwarz bound, gives
\[
 \Delta_{m,n}\le KB_{m,n}.                                            \tag{24}
\]
Equations (23)--(24) prove the corrected claim.  The original relation \(t_{m,n}\lesssim\Delta_{m,n}\) is false: if \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}=c\Sigma_{m,n}\) for \(c\ne1\), then \(\Delta_{m,n}=0\) but \(t_{m,n}=|\sqrt c-1|>0\).

Fix a prespecified mode and condition on \((\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})\).  Define
\[
 T_n=\max_{\ell\le H_n}\left|G_{m,n,\ell}/s_{m,n,\ell}\right|,
 \qquad F_n(x)=\Pr(T_n\le x\mid\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n}).
\]
The variance floor makes every marginal variance positive.  Thus \(F_n\) is continuous even if \(R_{m,n}\) is singular, because \(\{T_n=x\}\) lies in a finite union of zero-probability events \(\{|G_{m,n,\ell}|=xs_{m,n,\ell}\}\).

Let \(\widehat F_n\) be the multiplier distribution function and \(\widehat c_n\) its lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile.  On
\[
 \varepsilon_{m,n}\le e,\qquad t_{m,n}\le t<1/2,\qquad
 d_{m,n}\le d<\tfrac12\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\},                         \tag{25}
\]
put
\[
 c_-=F_n^{-1}(1-\alpha-d),\qquad c_+=F_n^{-1}(1-\alpha+d).
\]
The Kolmogorov bound gives \(c_-\le\widehat c_n\le c_+\), while Gaussian concentration gives \(c_+\le\kappa_{m,n}+C_\alpha\).  The expansion and scale inequalities imply the deterministic inclusions
\[
 \{T_n\le(1-t)c_- -e\}
 \subseteq\{\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\}
 \subseteq\{T_n\le(1+t)c_+ +e\}.                                     \tag{26}
\]
For example, the left inclusion follows coordinatewise from
\[
 |\widehat\theta_{m,n,\ell}-\theta_{n,\ell}|/s_{m,n,\ell}
 \le T_n+e\le(1-t)c_-
 \le\widehat c_n\widehat s_{m,n,\ell}/s_{m,n,\ell};
\]
the reverse triangle inequality proves the other inclusion.

The anti-concentration part of \(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}comparison\mbox{-}anticoncentration}\), applied to the two threshold displacements in (26), now gives
\[
 \left|\Pr(\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\mid
 \mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \le C_\alpha\{d+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)e+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t\}.             \tag{27}
\]
This uses deterministic \(F_n\)-quantile brackets, so it remains valid although the score and fitted covariance use common data.  Uniform convergence in probability supplies deterministic \(e,t,d\downarrow0\) for which the complement of (25) is uniformly negligible and the right side of (27) vanishes.  Averaging the already-uniform conditional conclusion over the selected layout proves the conditional-on-\(\mathcal F_n\) assertion.  No covariance inverse is used.

For the advertised horizon, the Gaussian union bound and tail integration give \(\kappa_{m,n}\le C\sqrt{\log(2H_n)}\) for every correlation matrix.  At \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), the two preceding theorems give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/2}\log n),
 &t_{\mathrm{dir},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}),\\
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-3/8}\log n+n^{-3/4}\log n),
 &t_{\mathrm{rec},n}\vee\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 &=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n}).
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{28}
\]
The comparison part of the cited lemma yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=O_{\Pr}\!\left(n^{-1/12}(\log n)^{5/6}\right)=o_{\Pr}(1),
\]
with a smaller direct error.  Multiplication by the displayed powers of \(\kappa_{m,n}+1\) shows that every term in the premise tends to zero.  Finally, simultaneous coverage implies pointwise coverage and, at \(H_n=1\), the construction equals the same Gaussian TWSF interval.  The strengthening concerns the whole conditional-mean path, not future realized prediction shocks.

Condition on \((\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})\).  All scores are centered Gaussian by \(\mathrm{thm{:}stacked\mbox{-}orthogonal\mbox{-}expansion}\).  Separate the lead-specific direct response error:
\[
 \frac{G_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}}
 =V_{n,\ell}+\sqrt{\nu_{n,\ell}}\,\xi_{n,\ell},                      \tag{29}
\]
where \(\xi_{n,1},\ldots,\xi_{n,H_n}\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables, independent of the centered Gaussian vector \(\boldsymbol V_n\).  This follows from \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\): the separated term is \(q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}e_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}/s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\), whose variance is \(\nu_{n,\ell}\), and the direct response blocks are mutually disjoint.

All \(a_{n,\ell}\) belong to the row space of \(\bar Z_{\mathrm{dir},n}\), of dimension at most \(r_0\), and all \(p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\) belong to the rank-\(r_{y,n}\) unit signal space.  In the covariance of \(\boldsymbol V_n\), the terminal and temporal-design contributions are scalar multiples of \((a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k})_{\ell,k}\), and the unit contribution is a scalar multiple of \((p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}p_{\mathrm{dir},n,k})_{\ell,k}\).  Hence, for a standard Gaussian \(Z_n\) of dimension at most \(2r_0\), there are vectors \(v_{n,\ell}\) such that
\[
 V_{n,\ell}=v_{n,\ell}^{\top}Z_n,\qquad
 \|v_{n,\ell}\|_2^2=1-\nu_{n,\ell}\le1.                              \tag{30}
\]
The triangle inequality gives
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}\le\mathbb E\|Z_n\|_2+\rho_n\le C+\rho_n.     \tag{31}
\]
Conversely, conditional on \((\xi_{n,\ell})_\ell\), the function
\[
 z\longmapsto\max_{\ell\le H_n}
 |v_{n,\ell}^{\top}z+\sqrt{\nu_{n,\ell}}\xi_{n,\ell}|
\]
is convex.  Jensen's inequality and \(\mathbb EZ_n=0\) give \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}\ge\rho_n\).  One standardized coordinate is \(N(0,1)\), so \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}\ge\sqrt{2/\pi}\).  Thus
\[
 c(1+\rho_n)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}\le C(1+\rho_n).               \tag{32}
\]

For recursion, the \(p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\beta,n}\) and \(q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}\) families lie in signal spaces of total dimension at most \(2r_0\).  After standardization their sum is \(u_{n,\ell}^{\top}\widetilde Z_n\), with \(\widetilde Z_n\) standard Gaussian of fixed dimension and \(\|u_{n,\ell}\|_2\le1\); its expected maximum is at most \(C\).  For the remaining terminal term, strong spectrum and bounded means give \(\|a_n\|_2+\|\beta_n\|_2\le K/\sqrt n\), while
\[
 g_{n,\ell}=\{\Pi_n(a_n)^{\ell-1}\}^{\top}a_n
\]
and stable short recursion give \(\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2\le K/\sqrt n\).  The variance floor therefore implies
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
 \frac{g_{n,\ell}^{\top}E_{W,n}^{\top}\beta_n}{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}
 \mathrel{\big|}\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n}\right)
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2\|\beta_n\|_2^2}
 {s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^2}\le K/n.                                 \tag{33}
\]
The Gaussian union bound gives expected maximum at most \(K\sqrt{\log(2H_n)/n}\).  Since \(H_n\le n^{1/8}\),
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}\le C.                                       \tag{34}
\]

Monotonicity of the heterogeneous maximum gives
\[
 \sqrt{\nu_{\min,n}}\,\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}|\xi_{n,\ell}|
 \le\rho_n\le
 \sqrt{\nu_{\max,n}}\,\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}|\xi_{n,\ell}|.     \tag{35}
\]
The Gaussian union bound gives the upper estimate \(C\sqrt{\log(2H_n)}\).  For the lower estimate, set \(x=c_0\sqrt{\log(2H_n)}\) with sufficiently small universal \(c_0>0\).  Mills' bound
\[
 \Pr(|\xi|>x)\ge c(1+x)^{-1}e^{-x^2/2}
\]
and independence imply
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|\xi_{n,\ell}|>x\right)
 =1-\{1-\Pr(|\xi|>x)\}^{H_n}\ge c.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E\max_\ell|\xi_{n,\ell}|\ge c\sqrt{\log(2H_n)}\), and (35) proves the two claimed bounds for \(\rho_n\).

Equation (32) makes direct complexity bounded exactly when \(\rho_n=O(1)\).  If all shares are zero, then \(\rho_n=0\).  If \(0<\nu_{\min,n}\le\nu_{\max,n}\le K\nu_{\min,n}\), (35) and (32) give
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}\asymp
 1+\sqrt{\nu_{\min,n}\log(2H_n)}.
\]
Every division is legal by the variance floor, and the constants depend only on the declared class radii.

Take all five dimensions equal to \(n\), singleton menus, disjoint fitting and terminal cells, and one forecast origin.  Give every donor and target loading one, every relevant mean time factor value one, and every primitive cell an independent \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\) error with the declared scale bounds.  Each mean design is an all-ones rank-one matrix with sole singular value \(n\); every mean is bounded, every relevant Hankel rank is one, and all recovery conditions hold because the mean vectors are multiples of \(\boldsymbol1_n\).  Also, for \(A_n=\Pi_n(\boldsymbol1_n/n)\),
\[
 \|A_n^j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(1+n^{-1/2})^j
 \le\exp(H_n/\sqrt n)=O(1),\qquad0\le j\le H_n.
\]
The variance calculation below gives the variance floor.  This constructs a member of \(\mathcal A_n\); its definition immediately gives \(\mathcal A_n\subset\mathcal C_n\).

The Moore--Penrose inverse of the \(n\)-by-\(n\) all-ones matrix is \(n^{-2}\boldsymbol1_n\boldsymbol1_n^{\top}\).  Therefore
\[
 \beta_n=a_n=a_{n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},
 \qquad q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n}.             \tag{36}
\]
Put \(c_{n,\ell}=(1+1/n)^{\ell-1}\).  The recursion
\[
 g_{n,1}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 g_{n,\ell+1}=S_n^{\top}g_{n,\ell}
 +\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n}(g_{n,\ell})_n
\]
gives by induction, for \(1\le\ell\le H_n<n\),
\[
 (g_{n,\ell})_i=
 \begin{cases}
 (c_{n,\ell}-c_{n,\ell-i})/n,&i<\ell,\\
 c_{n,\ell}/n,&i\ge\ell.
 \end{cases}
\]
Hence
\[
 \|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2=
 \frac{(n-\ell+1)c_{n,\ell}^2+
 \sum_{j=1}^{\ell-1}(c_{n,\ell}-c_{n,j})^2}{n^2}
 =\frac1n+O\!\left(\frac{H_n}{n^2}\right).                            \tag{37}
\]

Since \(A_n\boldsymbol1_n=\boldsymbol1_n\) and
\[
 e_n^{\top}A_n^je_n=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&j=0,\\
 n^{-1}(1+1/n)^{j-1},&1\le j<n,
 \end{cases}
\]
product differentiation in an arbitrary direction \(h\) gives
\[
 h^{\top}J_{n,\ell}^{\top}\boldsymbol1_n
 =\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}(e_n^{\top}A_n^je_n)
 h^{\top}A_n^{\ell-1-j}\boldsymbol1_n
 =c_{n,\ell}h^{\top}\boldsymbol1_n.
\]
Thus
\[
 J_{n,\ell}^{\top}\boldsymbol1_n=c_{n,\ell}\boldsymbol1_n,\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=c_{n,\ell}\boldsymbol1_n/n.                 \tag{38}
\]

Substitution in the score covariance formulas gives
\[
 s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2=\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}\left(2+\frac3n\right).
\]
The independent direct response contributes \(\sigma_n^2/n\), so
\[
 \nu_{n,\ell}=\nu_{\min,n}=\nu_{\max,n}=\frac1{2+3/n}.               \tag{39}
\]
The direct correlation is exactly equicorrelated:
\[
 R_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)
 =(1-\nu_n)+\nu_n\mathbf1\{\ell=k\},\qquad \nu_n=(2+3/n)^{-1}.       \tag{40}
\]
Thus its standardized coordinates equal
\[
 \sqrt{1-\nu_n}\,Z_0+\sqrt{\nu_n}\,Z_\ell,
\]
for independent standard normal \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_{H_n}\).  Since
\[
 \frac{\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_\ell|}{\sqrt{2\log H_n}}\longrightarrow1
\]
in probability and mean, the common term is negligible on the \(\sqrt{\log H_n}\) scale and \(\nu_n\to1/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}}{\sqrt{\log H_n}}\longrightarrow1,
\]
and the same probability sandwich makes every fixed-level maximum quantile divided by \(\sqrt{\log H_n}\) tend to one.

For recursion, set
\[
 U_n=p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\beta,n},\qquad
 V_n=n^{-1}\boldsymbol1_n^{\top}\delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}.
\]
They are independent, neither depends on \(\ell\), and each has variance \(\sigma_n^2(1+1/n)/n\).  Equations (37)--(38) give
\[
 G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}
 =U_n+c_{n,\ell}V_n+g_{n,\ell}^{\top}E_{W,n}^{\top}\beta_n,
\]
\[
 s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^2
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}
 \left[\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2+(1+1/n)(1+c_{n,\ell}^2)\right].            \tag{41}
\]
These direct and recursive variances are bounded below by \(c/n\), verifying the required floor.  Uniformly for \(\ell\le H_n\), \(c_{n,\ell}=1+O(H_n/n)\), and the standardized terminal term has marginal variance \(O(1/n)\).  A Gaussian union bound therefore shows that, for
\[
 Z_*=\frac{U_n+V_n}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(U_n+V_n)}}\sim N(0,1),
\]
\[
 \mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}
 \left|\frac{G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}-Z_*\right|
 \le K\left\{\frac{H_n}{n}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(2H_n)}n}\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.                                                    \tag{42}
\]
Thus \(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}\to\mathbb E|Z_*|=\sqrt{2/\pi}\).  The maximum also converges in probability to \(|Z_*|\); continuity and strict monotonicity of its distribution give the quantile limit \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).

By \(\mathrm{def{:}shen\mbox{-}singleton\mbox{-}embedding}\), every law in \(\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\) satisfies every member condition of \(\mathcal C_n\), has \(H_n=1\), and has singleton direct and recursive menus.  The identity map on observed blocks, target, and layout proves
\[
 \mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\subseteq
 \{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n:H_n=1,\
 |\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1\}.
\]
Selection is deterministic.  A one-dimensional correlation matrix with positive marginal variance is \((1)\), and the declared zero-variance fallback is also the one-dimensional identity.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
This exact equality implies the stated \(o_{\Pr}(1)\) formulation.  With \(H_n=1\), \(\mathrm{def{:}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) is precisely the selected-PCR pointwise TWSF interval centered and studentized by the same observed blocks.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}band}\) supplies its \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) conditional coverage.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(X\) and \(\widetilde X\) be centered Gaussian \(H_n\)-vectors with unit coordinate variances and maximum covariance discrepancy \(\Delta_{m,n}\), and apply the maximum results to their \(2H_n\) signed coordinates.  If \(T=\max_{\ell\le H_n}|X_\ell|\), \(\widetilde T=\max_{\ell\le H_n}|\widetilde X_\ell|\), and \(\kappa_{m,n}=\mathbb E T\), then, for a universal constant \(C\),
\[
 \sup_x\Pr\{|T-x|\le u\}\le C(\kappa_{m,n}+1)u,\qquad u>0,
\]
and
\[
 d_{m,n}\le
 \min\!\left\{1,C\Delta_{m,n}^{1/3}
 \left[1\vee\log\!\left(\frac{2H_n}{\Delta_{m,n}}\right)\right]^{2/3}\right\},
\]
with the right-hand side interpreted as zero when \(\Delta_{m,n}=0\).  These conclusions do not require \(R_{m,n}\) or \(\widehat R_{m,n}\) to be nonsingular.

source.locator: Theorems 2 and 3, applied to the signed coordinate vector

attestation.note: Stable arXiv handle supplied for the published comparison and anti-concentration statements used here.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The construction \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}\) is observable and positive semidefinite. Uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\),
\[
 \max_{\ell,k\le H_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)-\Sigma_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)|}
 {s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}s_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(nH_n)}n}\right),
\]
and the recursive analogue is
\[
 O_{\Pr}\!\left(H_n^2\sqrt{\frac{\log(nH_n)}n}\right).
\]
On the same event,
\[
 t_{m,n}\vee\Delta_{m,n}\lesssim
 \max_{\ell,k\le H_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)-\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)|}
 {s_{m,n,\ell}s_{m,n,k}}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The displayed relation between scale error and correlation error is false: multiplying every covariance entry by the same positive scalar changes all fitted standard deviations but leaves the correlation matrix unchanged. The proved normalization inequalities bound both errors by the relative covariance error, without ordering them against each other.

proposed.statement:
If \((\kappa_{m,n}+1)\varepsilon_{m,n}+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t_{m,n}+d_{m,n}=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), then
\[
 \sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n}
 \left|\Pr_{\mathbb P}(\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\mid\mathcal F_n)-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0
\]
for each prespecified mode \(m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\}\), with no lower eigenvalue condition on \(R_{m,n}\). The rates in Theorems \(\mathrm{thm{:}stacked\mbox{-}orthogonal\mbox{-}expansion}\) and \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rate}\), together with Gaussian comparison, verify the premise at \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). This strictly strengthens Shen's fixed-summary pointwise interval within the declared selected-training class by covering all \(H_n\) conditional means jointly.
proposed.justification: This is the headline feasible simultaneous-coverage result and explicitly accounts for remainder, studentization, and multiplier-law errors.
proposed.gap: Shen (2026, Corollary 2 and Section 6) gives pointwise inference for prespecified fixed-horizon summaries, while Belloni et al. (2018) does not derive the TWSF score and covariance inputs. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) compares direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts by asymptotic MSPE, but does not construct a causal selected-training score, a feasible cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon.
proposed.consumer: It turns the daily conditional-mean forecasts used in Shen's NFL-stadium analysis into one jointly interpretable path ribbon; cumulative paths require a separately transformed covariance audit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof invokes the published Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration result, so the theorem dependency is made explicit.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A legal sequence proving failure above the maximal exponent, and hence the exact value of the sharp exponent, is not derived.
open_obligations.obstruction: The recursive relative-Gram estimate is an upper perturbation bound. Its horizon-squared factor can result from the Jacobian Lipschitz bound and need not be attained by any member of the declared fixed-rank class. Therefore it cannot supply the lower failure sequence required by the open question.
open_obligations.attempted: The actual fitted three-piece temporal-Riesz decomposition and the persistent all-ones sequence were audited. They prove the stated upper rate, but the all-ones Jacobians align in one direction and do not yield a matching lower covariance error. No admissible fixed-rank alternative was found that both saturates the second-order companion perturbation and preserves the recovery, strong-spectrum, and power-boundedness conditions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Fix \(\gamma<1/4\), let \(H_n\le n^\gamma\), and put \(b_n=\log(nH_n)\).  The proved recursive rates imply
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}=O(1),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(\frac{H_nb_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{H_n^2b_n}{n}\right),
\]
\[
 t_{\mathrm{rec},n}\vee\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(H_n^2\sqrt{\frac{b_n}{n}}\right).
\]
The Gaussian comparison lemma gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(
 \Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(2H_n/\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n})\}^{2/3}\right)=o_{\Pr}(1).
\]
Because \(2\gamma-1/2<0\), all displayed polynomial rates dominate their logarithmic factors.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\),
\[
 (\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 +(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)^2t_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 +d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=o_{\Pr}(1).
\]
Thus achievability holds for every exponent below \(1/4\); the unresolved part is a matching legal failure sequence above the sharp boundary.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large even \(n\), condition on \(\mathcal F_n\), and abbreviate \(H=H_n\), \(\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol 1_n\), \(\boldsymbol v=\boldsymbol v_n\), and \(h_\ell=(-1)^\ell\).  By the definition of \(\boldsymbol v_n\),
\[
 \boldsymbol u^{\top}\boldsymbol v=0,
 \qquad \|\boldsymbol u\|_2^2=\|\boldsymbol v\|_2^2=n.
\]
Let
\[
 P=\frac{\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}}{n}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 B_n=\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}=nP.
\]
Thus \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}\), \(B_n\) has rank two, both its nonzero singular values equal \(n\), and
\[
 B_n^\dagger=\frac{P}{n}
 =\frac{\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}}{n^2}.
\]
Consequently the minimum-norm coefficients in the frozen definitions are
\[
 \beta_n=\frac{\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad
 a_{n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad
 a_n=\frac{\boldsymbol u-\boldsymbol v}{n}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \|\beta_n\|_2^2=\frac1n,
 \qquad
 a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}=\frac{1+h_\ell h_k}{n},
 \qquad
 \|a_n\|_2^2=\frac2n.
\]

We first verify membership in \(\mathcal C_n\).  The two deterministic factor coordinates \(1\) and \((-1)^j\), with unit loading vector \((1,(-1)^i)^{\top}\) at row \(i\), give
\[
 B_n(i,j)=1+(-1)^{i+j}.
\]
The target loading \((\cos(\varphi),\sin(\varphi))^{\top}\) gives \(\bar y_n(\varphi)=\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v\) and the future means
\[
 \theta_{n,\ell}=\cos(\varphi)+h_\ell\sin(\varphi).
\]
This is an explicit realization of the invariant-unit factor condition \(\mathrm{ass{:}factor\mbox{-}model}\).  Each of the two temporal factor coordinates has Hankel rank one, so the fixed Hankel-rank condition holds.  All five panel dimensions equal \(n\), all displayed signal matrices have rank two and nonzero singular values \(n\), and their entries, the response means, and the target means are bounded in absolute value by \(2\).  Hence the balanced-dimension, fixed-rank, strong-spectrum, and bounded-mean conditions hold with the fixed class envelopes containing this displayed rank-two construction.

Because
\[
 \operatorname{col}(B_n)=\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}
 =\operatorname{col}(B_n^{\top}),
\]
the unit-recovery condition holds.  Moreover,
\[
 B_na_{n,\ell}=\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v,
 \qquad
 B_na_n=\boldsymbol u-\boldsymbol v,
\]
so every direct response belongs to the selected temporal column space.  The direct terminal-transport equality is verified rather than assumed:
\[
 a_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n
 =a_{n,\ell}^{\top}B_n\beta_n
 =\frac{(\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v)^{\top}
 (\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v)}{n}
 =\cos(\varphi)+h_\ell\sin(\varphi)
 =\theta_{n,\ell}.
\]
For recursive recovery, every valid recurrence for the two factor sequences advances the constant coordinate to the constant coordinate and the alternating coordinate to its sign-flipped value.  Every advanced population terminal state therefore remains in \(\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}=\operatorname{col}(\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n})\), as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}recursive\mbox{-}recovery}\).

The minimum-norm recurrence also directly verifies short-horizon stability.  Write \(A=\Pi_n(a_n)=S_n+e_na_n^{\top}\).  Since \(n\) is even,
\[
 a_n^{\top}\boldsymbol u=1,
 \qquad a_n^{\top}\boldsymbol v=-1,
 \qquad S_n\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol u-e_n,
 \qquad S_n\boldsymbol v=-\boldsymbol v+e_n,
\]
and hence \(A\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol u\) and \(A\boldsymbol v=-\boldsymbol v\).  Also \(\|S_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) and \(\|e_na_n^{\top}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt{2/n}\), whence, for \(0\le j\le H\),
\[
 \|A^j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le (1+\sqrt{2/n})^j
 \le \exp(\sqrt2 H/\sqrt n)
 \le \exp(\sqrt2),
\]
where the last inequality uses \(H=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\le\sqrt n\).  Thus the stable-short-recursion condition holds with a constant independent of \(n\).

The training menus are singletons, so their measurable selections are deterministic.  The stipulated disjoint observed blocks and the i.i.d. Gaussian-cell construction give, respectively, independent selection, the required block independence, and conditionally i.i.d. \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\) primitive errors; the declared noise-scale condition supplies \(0<c_\sigma\le\sigma_n\le C_\sigma\).

It remains to verify the variance floor and calculate the direct covariance.  The population direct Riesz loadings reduce to
\[
 p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_na_{n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell},
 \qquad
 q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_n^{\top}\beta_n=\beta_n.
\]
For recursion, if \(g_{n,\ell}=(A^\ell)^{\top}e_n\), then
\[
 \boldsymbol u^{\top}g_{n,\ell}=e_n^{\top}A^\ell\boldsymbol u=1,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol v^{\top}g_{n,\ell}=e_n^{\top}A^\ell\boldsymbol v=h_\ell.
\]
It follows that
\[
 p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_ng_{n,\ell}
 =Pg_{n,\ell}
 =\frac{\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad \|p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2^2=\frac2n.
\]
The disjoint Gaussian response term \(p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}e_{y,n}\) is one summand of the recursive score, so independence of the primitive blocks yields
\[
 s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^2\ge
 \sigma_n^2\|p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2^2
 =\frac{2\sigma_n^2}{n}.
\]
The direct variance computed below is at least \(3\sigma_n^2/n\).  Together with \(\sigma_n\ge c_\sigma\), these inequalities verify the stated \(n^{-1/2}\) marginal variance floor.

For two direct leads \(\ell,k\), expand the score from \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\).  The Gaussian-cell and disjoint-block conditions imply that the terminal, unit-regression, and temporal-regression blocks are mutually independent; distinct direct response errors are also independent, whereas the same \(E_{Z,\mathrm{dir},n}\) is shared across leads.  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(G_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell},G_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}
 \mid\mathcal F_n)}{\sigma_n^2}
 =\|\beta_n\|_2^2a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}
 +(1+\|\beta_n\|_2^2)p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}p_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}
 +\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2^2
 \{\mathbf 1\{\ell=k\}+a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}\}.
\]
Substitution of the preceding identities gives the explicit covariance
\[
 \frac{\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\ell,k)}{\sigma_n^2}
 =\left(1+\frac3n\right)\frac{1+h_\ell h_k}{n}
 +\frac{\mathbf 1\{\ell=k\}}{n}.
\]
This expression is independent of \(\varphi\), and its diagonal is
\[
 s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2
 =\sigma_n^2\left(\frac3n+\frac6{n^2}\right).
\]
The last diagonal term is precisely the contribution \(q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}e_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\).  Its variance is \(\sigma_n^2\|\beta_n\|_2^2=\sigma_n^2/n\), and these contributions are independent over \(\ell\) and independent of all remaining score terms.  Its standardized variance share is consequently
\[
 \frac{\sigma_n^2/n}{\sigma_n^2(3/n+6/n^2)}=\frac1{3+6/n}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}I_H
 +\frac{\sigma_n^2(1+3/n)}{n}
 \bigl(\boldsymbol 1_H\boldsymbol 1_H^{\top}
 +\boldsymbol h_n\boldsymbol h_n^{\top}\bigr)
 \succeq \frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}I_H,
\]
so the covariance is positive definite.  Conditional on \(\mathcal F_n\), the score is a linear transformation of the stipulated primitive Gaussian errors and is therefore jointly Gaussian with mean zero and this covariance.  Since \(X_n=\boldsymbol\vartheta_n(\varphi)+\boldsymbol G_{\mathrm{dir},n}\),
\[
 X_n\mid\mathcal F_n\sim
 N\bigl(\boldsymbol\vartheta_n(\varphi),\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\boldsymbol 1_H\) and \(\boldsymbol h_n\) are linearly independent, so the curve indexed by \(\varphi\in[-\pi/6,\pi/6]\) is nonconstant; the covariance lower bound makes the experiment nondegenerate.  All defining conditions of \(\mathcal C_n\) have now been checked, proving \(\mathcal L_n\subset\mathcal C_n\) and all remaining assertions.

Fix \(0<\eta<1\), abbreviate
\[
 \nu_n=(3+6/n)^{-1},
 \qquad
 t_n=(1-\eta)\sqrt{2\nu_n\log H_n},
\]
and condition throughout on \(\mathcal F_n\).  By \(\mathrm{prop{:}legal\mbox{-}location\mbox{-}embedding}\), the standardized direct error
\[
 Z_{n,\ell}=\frac{G_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}}
\]
contains the mutually independent lead-response terms with variance share \(\nu_n\).  More explicitly, the score calculation in that proposition gives a decomposition
\[
 Z_{n,\ell}=R_{n,\ell}+\sqrt{\nu_n}\,\xi_{n,\ell},
 \qquad 1\le\ell\le H_n,
\]
where \(\xi_{n,1},\ldots,\xi_{n,H_n}\) are independent standard normal variables and are independent of the jointly Gaussian remainder \(\boldsymbol R_n\).  This decomposition uses the distinct direct lead-response cells; no independence among the coordinates of \(\boldsymbol R_n\) is asserted or needed.

We first establish a small-ball bound uniform over the value of the remainder.  If \(\xi\sim N(0,1)\), then for every \(x\ge0\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\), symmetry and monotonicity of the standard normal density imply
\[
 \Pr\{|\xi-b|<x\}\le \Pr\{|\xi|<x\}.
\]
Indeed, the probability on the left is the Gaussian mass of an interval of length \(2x\); differentiating that mass with respect to the nonnegative absolute displacement of its center shows that it is nonincreasing away from zero.  Conditional on \(\boldsymbol R_n\), independence of the \(\xi_{n,\ell}\)'s therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_{n,\ell}|<t_n
 \mathrel{\big|}\boldsymbol R_n,\mathcal F_n\right\}
 \le
 \left[\Pr\left\{|\xi|<\frac{t_n}{\sqrt{\nu_n}}\right\}\right]^{H_n}.
\]
Put \(x_n=(1-\eta)\sqrt{2\log H_n}\).  For \(x\ge1\), direct integration of the standard normal density \(\phi\) yields
\[
 \overline\Phi(x)
 =\int_x^\infty\phi(u)\,du
 \ge\int_x^{x+1/x}\phi(u)\,du
 \ge\frac1x\phi(x+1/x)
 \ge \frac{e^{-3/2}}{x}\phi(x).
\]
It follows that, for a universal \(c>0\),
\[
 2H_n\overline\Phi(x_n)
 \ge
 c\,\frac{H_n^{\,1-(1-\eta)^2}}{\sqrt{\log H_n}}
 =c\,\frac{H_n^{\,2\eta-\eta^2}}{\sqrt{\log H_n}}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Using \((1-u)^{H_n}\le e^{-H_nu}\) for \(0\le u\le1\), and then integrating the preceding conditional inequality over \(\boldsymbol R_n\), gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_{n,\ell}|<t_n
 \mathrel{\big|}\mathcal F_n\right\}
 \le \{1-2\overline\Phi(x_n)\}^{H_n}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The bound does not involve \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\), because the conditional error law and \(\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) are common to the entire location curve.

Now let \(C_n^{\mathrm{rect}}\in\mathfrak R_n\), and for a fixed \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) let
\[
 A_{n,\boldsymbol\vartheta}
 =\{\boldsymbol\vartheta\in C_n^{\mathrm{rect}}\}
\]
be its coverage event.  From the definition of the asymmetric rectangle, on this event one has, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 -W^+_{n,\ell}
 \le \frac{X_{n,\ell}-\vartheta_\ell}{s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}}
 \le W^-_{n,\ell}.
\]
Hence the deterministic event inclusion
\[
 A_{n,\boldsymbol\vartheta}\cap\{W_n^{\max}<t_n\}
 \subseteq
 \left\{\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_{n,\ell}|<t_n\right\}
\]
holds for every realization of both the data and the auxiliary randomization.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}
 \{W_n^{\max}\ge t_n\mid\mathcal F_n\}
 \ge
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}
 (A_{n,\boldsymbol\vartheta}\mid\mathcal F_n)
 -\Pr\left\{\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_{n,\ell}|<t_n
 \mid\mathcal F_n\right\}.
\]
The assumed uniform honesty bound and the preceding small-ball limit now imply
\[
 \inf_{\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}
 \left\{W_n^{\max}\ge
 (1-\eta)\sqrt{2(3+6/n)^{-1}\log H_n}
 \mathrel{\big|}\mathcal F_n\right\}
 \ge 1-\alpha-\delta_n-o(1).
\]
Finally \(W_n^{\max}\ge0\), so for every \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}
 [W_n^{\max}\mid\mathcal F_n]
 \ge t_n\,
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}
 \{W_n^{\max}\ge t_n\mid\mathcal F_n\}.
\]
Taking the infimum and applying the probability bound proves the asserted expected-width inequality.  The event inclusion was pointwise in asymmetric, data-dependent widths and in the independent randomizer, so all such widths are covered.  It also uses essentially that the rectangle is centered at \(X_n\); no claim has been made for an alternative center or an unrestricted estimator.
